analysis: The only changed line in docs/architecture/inference.md is line 1846, a documentation table row for the `stop` parameter. It now says stop strings match on held-back text via `StopHoldback`, and that GPT-OSS scopes matching to the Harmony `final` message through `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`. The provided units (head lines 1-416 and 417-805) are unchanged surrounding documentation, and the changed line itself is outside them. No code, configuration, authentication, encryption, cache or boundary behavior changes in this PR. The surrounding text covers Nemotron Super serving, cache scoping (T-041), SSD checkpoints and memory admission. I found no new attack surface or invalidated threat assumptions, and no threat-model entry needs updating. Stop-string scoping for GPT-OSS affects only output truncation semantics. It could in theory change what output a provider emits, but T-007 already treats provider output as untrusted. It does not touch the encryption or cache-scope trust boundaries. Remaining uncertainty: the code the doc row describes (`ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, `StopHoldback`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) was not supplied, so I could not verify that the documentation matches the implementation, or that the scoped matching has no security effect, for example stop-sequence leakage of analysis or tool-call content. This is a documentation-only change.
